modern:
Attend to the matter in front of you, whether it is an opinion or an act or a word.

You suffer this justly: for you would rather become good tomorrow than be good today.
original:
Attend to the matter which is before thee, whether it is an opinion or an act or a word.

Thou sufferest this justly: for thou choosest rather to become good to-morrow than to be good to-day.
notification: Attend to the matter in front of you, whether it is an opinion or an act or a word.
notification_original: Attend to the matter which is before thee, whether it is an opinion or an act or a word.

explained.summary: Two notes to self. Pay attention to what’s actually in front of you, whether it’s a thought, an action or a word. And a sharper one: you’re suffering this for good reason, because you’d rather become good tomorrow than be good today. Marcus is calling out his own procrastination about becoming a better person.
explained.today: It’s the ’I’ll start being patient once this busy patch is over’ or ’I’ll call Mum properly when things calm down’. The chance to act well is always today’s conversation, not the improved version of you next month.
